questions.a: Measurement tells exactly how long, heavy or hot something is - guesswork is not enough.

questions.q: Name three quantities we measure daily.
What is wrong with measuring cloth by hand-span?
questions.a: Hand-spans differ from person to person, so the result is not the same for everyone.

questions.q: State the standard units of length and their relations.
questions.a: Metre is standard; 1 km = 1000 m, 1 m = 100 cm, 1 cm = 10 mm.

questions.q: Which unit will you use for your height and why?
questions.a: Centimetre (or metre) - convenient numbers for a person's height.

questions.q: Why is the metre called a standard unit?
questions.a: It is fixed internationally and gives the same measure everywhere.

concepts.title: Describing Position and Types of Motion

questions.q: What is position and how do we describe it?
questions.a: Position is the location of an object compared to a reference point, with distance and direction.

questions.q: Name three types of motion with examples.
questions.a: Straight-line (car on road), circular (fan blade), periodic (pendulum).

questions.q: When do we say an object is at rest?
questions.a: When its position does not change with time relative to its surroundings.
